items.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: they called it traditional jazz because it was going back to the roots, the early Armstrong, Oliver, Bunk Johnson and the early New Orleans type people

ctx.x: Gee I hope they had that in a frame on a wall somewhere.

I think it’s somewheres in some of those books. But the word “trad” was kind of, they called it traditional jazz because it was going back to the roots, the early Armstrong, Oliver, Bunk Johnson and the early New Orleans type people, which is a lot different than the music of George Lewis and some of those other black musicians that started performing in the 40s. It was a little more complicated in the early days. They played some arrangements and things if you listen to Louis Armstrong’s “Hot Five” and “Hot…
And is it the Chicago days? Is it associated with the city?
